CUT FROM specled_-k6s (2026-07-27) by user decision. NOT closed, NOT descoped - deferred to its own PR.

Cold verification says the mandate is still fully applicable (verdict: still_applicable, effort: medium). It was excluded from the single-PR fast-follow epic for two reasons the verifier surfaced:

1. SELF-GATE RISK. Wiring CrossField into the live decision-parse path fires cross_field/affects_unresolved on 5 shipped repo.governance ADRs and flattens 9 missing_change_type warnings into hard errors (verifier.ex:1894-1898), which violates specled.decisions.change_type_optional. Landing it inside a 21-ticket PR means remediating specled own governance corpus mid-PR.
2. ONLY HASH-MOVER. It is the only ticket in the candidate set that moves .spec/realization_hashes.json entries (CrossField.validate/3, DecisionParser.parse_file/4, Verifier.verify_decision/4). Cutting it lets the epic forbid every agent from touching the baseline outright instead of regenerating mid-flight.

SEQUENCING FOR THE FOLLOW-UP PR: specled_-14t stays in specled_-k6s and lands first. Its ruling on the repo. affect-prefix carve-out determines whether 4a6 adds a carve-out or migrates the 5 ADRs - so do not start 4a6 until k6s has merged and 14t resolution is readable in the tree.

== SCOPED REMAINING WORK (preserved from admission verification) ==
Pick and execute ONE of the two options. Both are blocked on the same two hazards that a naive wiring would trip; the implementer must handle them or `mix spec.check` breaks on specled's own 50 ADRs.

OPTION A (wire it — preferred, keeps the requirement text as written):
A1. lib/specled_ex/index.ex `build/2`: split decision parsing into two passes. Keep line 31 producing `decisions` with `current_index = nil`, build `base_index` (lines 33-42) as today, then replace the `"decisions"` value with `DecisionParser.validate_cross_fields(decisions, base_index, opts)` before `maybe_add_tag_data/3`. `CrossField.resolvable_ids/1` (cross_field.ex:288) reads `current_index["subjects"]` / `["decisions"]` and `subject["requirements"]`, so `base_index` is already the right shape — no new struct needed.
A2. HAZARD 1 — `repo.*` affects. 5 shipped ADRs (specled.decision.{explicit_subject_ownership, declarative_current_truth, file_backed_linked_strength, guided_reconciliation_loop, local_skill_scaffold}.md) carry `affects: [repo.governance]`. The Verifier accepts these via `String.starts_with?(affect, "repo.")` (verifier.ex:2100) but `CrossField.resolvable_ids/1` does not, so wiring as-is emits 5 `cross_field/affects_unresolved` ERRORS. Add the same `repo.`-prefix carve-out (and the `claim_ids` source) to `CrossField.apply_rule(:r4_affects_resolve, ...)` at cross_field.ex:145-172 so the two paths agree exactly, and state the carve-out in the `cross_field_affects_resolve` requirement text at .spec/specs/decision_governance.spec.md:101-110.
A3. HAZARD 2 — warning severity is flattened to error. lib/specled_ex/verifier.ex:1894-1898 `add_decision_parse_error_findings/5` does `[finding("error", "decision_parse_error", message, ...)]` for EVERY `parse_errors` string, and decision_parser.ex:74-76 encodes warnings as the plain string `"warning #{code}: #{message}"`. R7 (`cross_field/missing_change_type`, cross_field.ex:175-188) fires for 9 shipped ADRs that have no `change_type:` line (declarative_current_truth, evidence_based_attribution, explicit_subject_ownership, file_backed_linked_strength, file_touch_yields_to_realization, guided_reconciliation_loop, local_skill_scaffold, no_app_start, spec_review_html_viewer), so wiring as-is turns 9 warnings into 9 hard errors — directly violating .spec/specs/decision_governance.spec.md:57-64 (`specled.decisions.change_type_optional`: "shall parse successfully and emit a `cross_field/missing_change_type` warning-level diagnostic rather than a parse error"). Carry severity structurally (e.g. a separate `"parse_warnings"` key on the decision map, or a `{severity, message}` tuple) and emit `finding("warning", "decision_cross_field_warning", ...)` for those; `finding/5` already takes severity as its first argument so `"warning"` is expressible.
A4. Add an integration test (new or in an index-level test) proving `Index.build/2` output carries a `cross_field/affects_unresolved` error for an unresolvable non-deprecates affect and does NOT for a `deprecates` one — i.e. R4/R6 exercised through the live path, not only through direct `CrossField.validate/3` calls.
A5. Either delete `validate_cross_fields/3` (decision_parser.ex:58-62) or make A1 its single caller; do not leave it dead.

OPTION B (re-scope): rewrite .spec/specs/decision_governance.spec.md:101-110 so `cross_field_affects_resolve` names the live enforcer (`SpecLedEx.Verifier.verify_decision/4` / `valid_decision_affect?/4`) rather than "the CrossField validator", add `SpecLedEx.Verifier.verify_decision/4`-backed tagged tests to the covers list, and delete the unreachable `current_index` plumbing (decision_parser.ex:58-62 and the `parse_file/4` `current_index` parameter) so no dead gate remains. Note this makes `CrossField` a partially-vestigial module and needs an ADR in .spec/decisions/ recording the consolidation.

== RISK NOTES ==
REALIZATION-HASH DRIFT: yes, near-certain. .spec/realization_hashes.json carries api_boundary entries for "SpecLedEx.DecisionParser.CrossField.validate/3" (line 351) and "SpecLedEx.DecisionParser.parse_file/4" (line 355), plus an implementation entry for "SpecLedEx.Verifier.verify_decision/4" (line 651) — all three are bindings this work edits, and per prior experience api_boundary hashes are line-position-sensitive, so even non-semantic edits above those functions in decision_parser.ex / cross_field.ex / verifier.ex will drift them. The baseline must be regenerated as part of the ticket, and in a 22-ticket single-PR landing the regeneration MUST be done once at the end by the orchestrator, not per-ticket, or the hash file will conflict repeatedly.

HARD ORDERING DEPENDENCY on specled_-14t: 14t is "Document or remove the unverified 'repo.' affect-prefix exemption in Verifier.valid_decision_affect?/4" — the exact function (lib/specled_ex/verifier.ex:2095-2101) and the exact `String.starts_with?(affect, "repo.")` clause that step A2 above must mirror into CrossField. If 14t REMOVES the exemption, A2's carve-out must not be added and instead the 5 `repo.governance` ADRs must be migrated first; if 14t DOCUMENTS it, A2 must copy it. Land 14t first, or merge the two tickets. Do not implement 4a6 blind to 14t's outcome.

SOFT CONFLICT with specled_-vbo: also edits lib/specled_ex/verifier.ex, but in the workflow_file verification region (~L706 per its description), not the decision-finding region (L1811-1930, L2095-2101). Different hunks; textual merge should be clean, but both will contend for the verifier.ex realization hash.

SPEC-REQUIREMENT CONTENTION: this ticket edits .spec/specs/decision_governance.spec.md requirement `specled.decisions.cross_field_affects_resolve` (:101-110) and interacts with `specled.decisions.change_type_optional` (:57-64). specled_-14t also targets ADR-affect resolution semantics and may want to touch `specled.decisions.reference_validation` (:38-45) in the same file. Reserve decision_governance.spec.md for the 4a6+14t pair.

SELF-GATE RISK: this is the rare ticket that can turn specled's own `mix spec.check` red on merge. Both hazards (5 `repo.governance` errors, 9 missing-`change_type` warnings-flattened-to-errors) fire on the repo's OWN 50 ADRs in .spec/decisions/. Run `mix spec.check --no-run-commands` after wiring and BEFORE assuming the ticket is done; a green pre-wiring gate says nothing.

ADR SURFACE: .spec/decisions/specled.decision.deprecates_affect_reference_carveout.md:19-25 and :44 explicitly reason about the CrossField-vs-live-verifier gap ("something stricter than both CrossField and the live verifier now enforce"; "The current-truth requirement matches CrossField and verifier"). Whichever option is chosen, that ADR's prose must be re-read and likely amended — and ADRs are append-only under CrossField R5 (cross_field.ex:193-255), so amend by superseding, not by editing `affects`/`change_type`/`reverses_what` in place.

Confirmed again by the 2026-08-12 five-persona critical review (SPEC-H1), independently traced twice: Index.build calls DecisionParser.parse_file/2 (decision_parser.ex:9-11), which passes current_index = nil; maybe_run_cross_field(decision, nil, _opts) returns the decision untouched (:64). validate_cross_fields/3 has no caller in lib/, and no mix task references DecisionParser or CrossField at all. All six cross_field_* must requirements are enforced only by their own unit tests. NEW EVIDENCE: release 0.15.0 shipped three narrows-scope ADRs with no reverses_what — a combination specled.decisions.cross_field_reverses_what says 'shall emit an error' — and spec.check returned result=pass. They were corrected by hand in commit e71ac7bc, but the gate did not catch them. This is the first tree where the dead validator demonstrably let a real governance violation through.

THIRD INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION — first from a downstream adopter, plus a correction to step A1 and a live violation in this repo's own corpus.

Filed from: drovr (github.com/iautom8things/drovr), ticket drv-3t8, 2026-08-14.

== A1 IS WRONG AS WRITTEN — base_index is NOT the right shape ==

A1 says: "CrossField.resolvable_ids/1 reads current_index["subjects"] / ["decisions"] and subject["requirements"], so base_index is already the right shape — no new struct needed."

It is not. Parser.parse_file stores a %SpecLedEx.Schema.Meta{} STRUCT under subject["meta"] on the success path (parser.ex:57-59, via Schema.validate_block("spec-meta", meta)), while resolvable_ids/1 reads the id with a STRING key through get_in_nested(subject, ["meta", "id"]) (cross_field.ex:288-298). Map.get(%Meta{}, "id") is nil, so EVERY subject id resolves to nil and every affects entry naming a subject or requirement looks unresolved.

Measured on this tree (HEAD c228bff7, `mix run --no-start`, Index.build then CrossField.validate against the index as-is):

  subject meta is_struct=true
  string-key id lookup => nil
  decisions=36 subjects=33
  %{"cross_field/affects_unresolved" => 36,
    "cross_field/missing_change_type" => 9,
    "cross_field/reverses_what_missing" => 1}

So naive wiring emits affects_unresolved on all 36 ADRs, not the 5 repo.governance ones HAZARD 1 predicts. This is a THIRD hazard, independent of the other two, and it is the one that makes the wiring look catastrophically broken on first run. Note the inversion it creates: an INVALID spec-meta falls to parser.ex:62-63, which stores the raw string-keyed map, so ids from BROKEN specs resolve while ids from valid ones do not.

Whichever option is chosen, either normalize subject meta at the call site before handing the index to CrossField, or make resolvable_ids/1 struct-aware. drovr's local workaround normalizes at the call site (Map.from_struct + Atom.to_string on keys) and pins the behavior in both directions — a resolve test and a reject test — because a normalizer that declares everything resolvable passes a resolve-only assertion.

== THIS REPO'S OWN CORPUS HAS A LIVE R2 VIOLATION RIGHT NOW ==

.spec/decisions/specled.decision.parser_resilient_errors_split.md carries change_type: narrows-scope (a weakening type) with no reverses_what. specled.decisions.cross_field_reverses_what says the validator "shall emit an error" for exactly that. On the same tree, `mix spec.check --no-run-commands` reports `status=pass errors=0 warnings=0`, exit 0.

That is now the second such escape in this repo after the three 0.15.0 narrows-scope ADRs noted on 2026-08-12, and this one is still in the tree rather than hand-corrected. Add it to the remediation list for whichever option lands.

== DOWNSTREAM EVIDENCE (drovr, pinned at bb64e69) ==

drovr hit the same gap from the outside and had to build its own gate. Sequence:

1. A five-persona critical review of drovr's drv-6pr found a malformed ADR by hand (finding F17) — an ADR that R2 classifies as a hard error, while `mix spec.check --no-run-commands` reported errors=0 warnings=0 on it.
2. drv-3t8 confirmed the cause: on the pinned tree, Index.build calls DecisionParser.parse_file/2 (index.ex:31), that arity passes current_index=nil (decision_parser.ex:9-11), and maybe_run_cross_field(decision, nil, _) returns the decision untouched (:64). validate_cross_fields/3 has zero callers in lib/. verifier.ex contains no cross_field reference at all. Same as reported here on 2026-08-12; independently re-traced.
3. Live repro, run by a cold verifier on drovr's tree: a NEW ADR with change_type: weakens and no reverses_what → `mix spec.check --no-run-commands` says `validate status=pass errors=0 warnings=0`, `spec.check result=pass`. Same file switched to change_type: supersedes with no replaces → also pass.
4. Contrast confirming only R4 is duplicated by the Verifier: the same ADR with an unresolvable affects id → spec.check FAILS with `[ERROR] decision_unknown_affect`. So of the classes drovr cared about, affects-resolve was already covered and R1/R2 were genuinely blind.

drovr's fix (test/spec/adr_cross_field_test.exs, commit ed54e2f) runs CrossField over its ADR corpus from its own test suite, so `mix test` and therefore `make gates` enforce it. Every enforced rule is driven by a fixture ADR written to a tmp dir and read back through DecisionParser.parse_file/2; a cold verifier mutation-proved each of R1 (both branches), R2, R3, R4 and R7 red-lights exactly its own test. That is a workaround, not a fix — every adopter needs the same ~250 lines, and each one will independently trip the struct-meta trap above.

== SUGGESTED PRIORITY ==

Raising P3 -> P2. Three independent traces, two demonstrated escapes in this repo, one demonstrated escape plus a full workaround ticket in a downstream adopter. Six must requirements remain enforced only by their own unit tests. Not P1 only because the hazards are real and the remediation is genuinely multi-step, exactly as scoped above.

Summary: Option A of the charter. Index.build/2 parses ADRs in two passes and runs CrossField.validate/3 over each one against the index built from the same tree, so the six cross_field_* must requirements now gate mix spec.check instead of only their own unit tests. Cross-field severity is carried structurally — errors into parse_errors, warnings into a new parse_warnings list the verifier reports as decision_cross_field_warning at info — because spec.check validates with strict: true, where a warning is fatal and would break every workspace holding a change_type-less legacy ADR that specled.decisions.change_type_optional exists to protect. New requirement specled.decisions.cross_field_live_gate plus ADR specled.decision.live_cross_field_gate record the wiring and the severity mapping.

DEVIATIONS AND FINDINGS BEYOND THE CHARTER (all confirmed by execution, not inspection):

1. The charter's hazard A2 was already resolved. specled_-14t landed the repo. carve-out in both the requirement text and CrossField R4 (reject_repo_namespace/1), so no carve-out work was needed here.

2. NEW: CrossField had never met a real index. resolvable_ids/1 read subject["meta"]["id"] with string keys, but Index.build/2 emits schema structs with atom keys, so ZERO subject ids resolved. Wiring as-is produced 55 cross_field/affects_unresolved errors against correct ADRs — an order of magnitude past the 5 the charter predicted, and none of them repo.*. Every R4 fixture was a hand-built plain map, which is exactly why nothing caught it. Fixed with a key-agnostic accessor; the resolvable set now also includes scenario ids, matching what Verifier.valid_decision_affect?/4 accepts (charter step A2's claim_ids clause).

3. NEW: 4 shipped ADRs (amplification_scoped_dedupe, doc_identifier_lint_spec_corpus, parser_resilient_errors_split, resolution_path_provenance) declare a weakening-set change_type with no reverses_what — the same class as the 0.15.0 escape, 4 more instances. They could not be repaired: append_only.ex:496 compared reverses_what verbatim and emitted append_only/adr_affects_widened at error for any difference, so the only legal remedy was superseding 4 records whose decisions are correct, and every adopter would hit the same wall on upgrade. Per user decision (asked mid-implementation, options: backfill carve-out / supersede all 4 / drop R2 from the live gate) the carve-out was chosen: new requirement specled.append_only.adr_reverses_what_backfill + ADR specled.decision.adr_reverses_what_backfill make blank -> non-blank exempt while change_type and affects stay compared verbatim and any edit to an existing value is still drift. Real justification prose was then backfilled into all 4.

4. Charter step A5 (do not leave validate_cross_fields/3 dead): Index.build/2 is now its single caller. parse_file/4 remains the production parse entry point via parse_file/2.

5. Realization hashes did NOT drift — the charter predicted near-certain drift on CrossField.validate/3, DecisionParser.parse_file/4, and Verifier.verify_decision/4. mix spec.check --no-run-commands --verbose reports no branch_guard_realization_drift finding at any severity, so .spec/realization_hashes.json is untouched and needs no regeneration.

6. Two branch_guard_missing_subject_update errors were downgraded via a Spec-Drift: branch_guard_missing_subject_update=info commit trailer: verifier.ex impacts specled.prose_guard and index_state_test.exs impacts specled.package / specled.status, none of whose contracts this change moves. The three subjects whose contracts DID move were updated properly instead: specled.decisions (new requirement), specled.index_state (summary gained decision_parse_warnings; two-pass parse), specled.verify.decision_governance (the new finding channel and its severity).

7. Advisory append_only/statement_rewritten warnings remain for the three amended requirements. They are the intended signal for a reviewed in-place clarification, not a gate failure.

No must requirement, scenario, or success criterion was deferred; no follow-up tickets were filed.
